quests.question: Nothing ___ ever easy at the start of a new project.
quests.hint: 'Nothing' is singular - use the singular form of 'be'.
quests.explanation: 'Nothing' is a singular indefinite pronoun. 'Nothing is ever easy' - the verb is always singular with 'nothing'.

quests.question: Everything on these shelves ___ half price today.
quests.hint: 'Everything' is singular - even though it refers to many items.
quests.explanation: 'Everything' is always singular, regardless of how many items it refers to. 'Everything is half price' - not 'are'.

quests.question: Few people ___ that this problem has an easy solution.
quests.hint: 'Few people' is plural - use the base form of the verb.
quests.explanation: 'Few people' is plural. 'Few' indicates a small number and takes a plural verb: 'few people believe'.

quests.question: Many a student ___ struggled with this concept.
quests.hint: 'Many a' is followed by a singular noun and takes a singular verb.
quests.explanation: 'Many a' is a fixed formal expression followed by a singular noun. Despite the meaning of 'many', the verb is always singular: 'many a student has struggled'.

quests.question: A great many students ___ signed up for the new course.
quests.hint: 'A great many students' is plural - 'students' controls the verb.
quests.explanation: 'A great many' is always followed by a plural noun and takes a plural verb: 'a great many students have signed up'.

quests.question: Each student in the class ___ a copy of the textbook.
quests.hint: 'Each student' is singular - 'each' always makes the subject singular.
quests.explanation: 'Each' always takes a singular verb, no matter how many students there are. 'Each student has a copy' - not 'have'.

quests.question: Either of these routes ___ you to the city centre.
quests.hint: 'Either' as a subject pronoun is singular.
quests.explanation: When 'either' stands alone as a subject (not part of 'either…or'), it is singular and takes a singular verb: 'either takes'.

quests.question: Neither of the reports ___ complete.
quests.hint: 'Neither' as a subject pronoun is singular.
quests.explanation: When 'neither' stands alone as a subject, it is singular and takes a singular verb: 'neither of the reports is complete'.

quests.question: A lot of effort ___ needed to master a language.
quests.hint: 'A lot of effort' - 'effort' is uncountable, so the verb is singular.
quests.explanation: 'Effort' is uncountable. When 'a lot of' precedes an uncountable noun, the verb is singular: 'a lot of effort is needed'.

quests.question: A lot of students ___ struggling with the new curriculum.
quests.hint: 'A lot of students' - 'students' is plural, so the verb is plural.
quests.explanation: When 'a lot of' precedes a countable plural noun, the verb is plural: 'a lot of students are struggling'.

quests.question: Plenty of time ___ still available before the deadline.
quests.hint: 'Plenty of time' - 'time' is uncountable, so the verb is singular.
quests.explanation: When 'plenty of' precedes an uncountable noun like 'time', the verb is singular: 'plenty of time is available'.

quests.question: Plenty of seats ___ still available for tonight's show.
quests.hint: 'Plenty of seats' - 'seats' is countable and plural, so the verb is plural.
quests.explanation: When 'plenty of' precedes a countable plural noun like 'seats', the verb is plural: 'plenty of seats are available'.

quests.question: More than one student ___ failed to complete the assignment.
quests.hint: 'More than one' always takes a singular verb.
quests.explanation: 'More than one', despite meaning several, always takes a singular verb. 'More than one student has failed' - this is a fixed grammatical convention.

quests.question: The number of complaints ___ increased significantly.
quests.hint: The phrase 'the number of' is singular - it counts as one thing.
quests.explanation: Remember: 'the number of' is singular (it describes one total), while 'a number of' is plural (meaning 'several'). 'The number of complaints has increased'.

quests.question: A number of issues ___ raised during the meeting.
quests.hint: 'A number of' means 'several' and takes a plural verb.
quests.explanation: 'A number of' means 'several' and always takes a plural verb. 'A number of issues were raised' - not 'was raised'.

quests.question: The rest of the money ___ donated to charity.
quests.hint: 'The rest of the money' - 'money' is uncountable, so the verb is singular.
quests.explanation: 'Money' is uncountable. 'The rest of the money was donated' - the verb is singular because the noun is uncountable.

quests.question: The rest of the staff ___ offered voluntary redundancy.
quests.hint: 'The rest of the staff' (individuals) is plural here - plural verb.
quests.explanation: Here, 'the rest of the staff' refers to the individual employees, not the group as a unit. 'Staff members were offered' - plural verb for plural individuals.

quests.question: Much of the damage ___ already repaired.
quests.hint: 'Much of the damage' - 'damage' is uncountable, so the verb is singular.
quests.explanation: 'Damage' is uncountable. 'Much of the damage was repaired' - uncountable nouns take singular verbs, even with 'much of'.

quests.question: Much of what he said ___ true.
quests.hint: 'Much of what he said' is a singular noun phrase - singular verb.
quests.explanation: The subject here is 'much of what he said', which functions as a singular noun phrase. It takes a singular verb: 'was true'.

quests.question: Many of the recommendations ___ accepted.
quests.hint: 'Many of the recommendations' - 'recommendations' is plural, so the verb is plural.
quests.explanation: 'Many of' followed by a plural noun takes a plural verb. 'Many of the recommendations were accepted'.

quests.question: Few of the options ___ realistic given our budget.
quests.hint: 'Few of the options' - 'options' is plural, and 'few' is also plural.
quests.explanation: 'Few' refers to a small plural number. 'Few of the options are realistic' - plural noun and plural indefinite pronoun both signal a plural verb.

quests.question: Not one of the solutions ___ adequate.
quests.hint: 'Not one' is singular - it picks out a single item from a group.
quests.explanation: 'Not one' acts like 'none' in singular usage. 'Not one of the solutions is adequate' - the verb is singular.

quests.question: Somebody in the audience ___ shouting.
quests.hint: 'Somebody' is singular - even in an audience of thousands.
quests.explanation: 'Somebody' is always singular. 'Somebody was shouting' - the verb is singular even though there may be many people in the audience.

quests.question: Everyone except the late arrivals ___ seated.
quests.hint: 'Everyone' is the subject - it is always singular.
quests.explanation: The subject is 'everyone', which is always singular. The phrase 'except the late arrivals' does not change the subject. 'Everyone was seated'.

quests.question: Either of the two doctors ___ available to see you.
quests.hint: 'Either of' as a subject is singular - it refers to one at a time.
quests.explanation: 'Either of' followed by a plural noun is still singular in standard English. 'Either of the two doctors is available' - not 'are'.

quests.question: Neither of the medications ___ working effectively.
quests.hint: 'Neither of' as a subject is singular in formal English.
quests.explanation: 'Neither of' followed by a plural noun is treated as singular in formal English. 'Neither of the medications is working'.

quests.question: Both of the candidates ___ well prepared.
quests.hint: 'Both of' is always plural - 'both' refers to two things together.
quests.explanation: 'Both of' is always plural. 'Both of the candidates are well prepared' - unlike 'either' and 'neither', 'both' always takes a plural verb.

quests.question: Enough food ___ prepared for the whole group.
quests.hint: 'Food' is uncountable - singular verb with 'enough'.
quests.explanation: 'Food' is uncountable, so 'enough food was prepared' is correct. Uncountable nouns take singular verbs regardless of the quantity word before them.

quests.question: Enough chairs ___ arranged for all the guests.
quests.hint: 'Chairs' is countable and plural - plural verb with 'enough'.
quests.explanation: 'Chairs' is a countable plural noun, so 'enough chairs were arranged' is correct. Plural countable nouns take plural verbs.

quests.question: The amount of paperwork ___ overwhelming.
quests.hint: 'The amount of' with an uncountable noun takes a singular verb.
quests.explanation: 'The amount of' is similar to 'the number of' - it is singular. 'The amount of paperwork was overwhelming'. Compare with 'the number of reports was high'.
